strings.name: Bob Metcalfe
strings.summary: Educated at MIT and Harvard, Metcalfe worked on early ARPANET connections. At Xerox PARC, he developed Ethernet with David Boggs and colleagues, then cofounded 3Com and helped promote network standards and commercial products. His career also includes technology writing, venture investment and university entrepreneurship education. Announced in 2023, the 2022 Turing Award recognized his contributions to Ethernet’s invention, standardization and commercialization.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped invent Ethernet and advance its standardization and commercial application, profoundly influencing local networks and modern network infrastructure.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: MIT bachelor’s degrees in electrical engineering and industrial management (1969); Harvard doctorate in applied mathematics (1973).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Developing Ethernet
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed local networking with Boggs and a team, enabling data communication between personal computers.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Standards and commercialization
strings.highlights.h2.text: Promoted Ethernet products through 3Com and industry cooperation, helping turn networking into shared infrastructure.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Receiving the 2022 Turing Award
strings.timeline.t1.text: ACM announced the award for Ethernet invention, standardization and commercialization.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Teaching entrepreneurship
strings.timeline.t2.text: Joined the University of Texas at Austin as a professor of innovation and entrepreneurship.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Advancing an Ethernet industry standard
strings.timeline.t3.text: Helped connect DEC, Intel and Xerox in developing the DIX Ethernet specification.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Cofounding 3Com
strings.timeline.t4.text: Founded a networking company that brought Ethernet interfaces and related products to market.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Publishing the Ethernet paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published a local-network packet-switching paper with Boggs explaining Ethernet’s design.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Writing the Ethernet memo
strings.timeline.t6.text: Proposed a network connecting Alto computers at Xerox PARC and worked on implementation with colleagues.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earning a Harvard doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed doctoral training in applied mathematics, with research involving early computer networks.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing MIT studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned bachelor’s degrees in electrical engineering and industrial management before continuing networking research.
